archetype.name: Pocket Passer (veteran backup)
archetype.definition: A big-framed, 11th-year pocket thrower whose game has always been timing and arm talent rather than escapability, now a spot starter whose legs no longer bail out protection breakdowns.

report.headline: One good relief half, then an accuracy collapse that landed him at QB3
report.take:
Wentz's 2026 is three appearances spread across eight weeks: an 83%-snap relief outing against Green Bay in Week 1, a start in a 9-3 win at Chicago, and a start against Buffalo in Week 9 that went badly enough that Kirk Cousins started Week 10. As of November 17 he is listed third on the depth chart behind Cousins, with Kyler Murray out with a hamstring strain. Read the card as a backup's audition, not a starter's season.

The season splits sharply. The Green Bay relief game was the good part: 12 of 19, three touchdowns and +5.1 passing EPA. As a starter he is 19 of 45 for 224 yards with no touchdowns, two picks and -0.374 EPA per dropback. That is a bottom-of-the-league rate, and the Buffalo game produced most of it: 8 of 25, -18.4 EPA, a -30.7 CPOE and a 41.7% bad-throw rate. On a 64-attempt sample, one game like that sinks a season line, and it did. His -15.41 CPOE ranks 53rd of 54 qualifiers.

The numbers point to two causes. The first is accuracy. His bad-throw rate is 28.1%, last among 42 charted passers and up 9.2 points from last year's 18.9%. His career bad-throw ranks have usually sat in the bottom half, but nothing like this. The second is approach. His aggressiveness is 20.31% against 14.8% last season, and against Buffalo it hit 32% with a 10.4-yard intended air distance, so he was forcing tight-window throws to chase a game. Throws over the middle have actually worked (+0.145 EPA, 65% completions). Outside the numbers he has been off target to both sides, with right-side throws at -0.271 EPA. The running that once covered for him is gone: 0.56 yards per carry and designed runs at -1.376 EPA. At 33.9 that is probably age, not noise.

The 2025 baseline is the counterweight. In five games for this same team he completed 65.1%, averaged 7.2 yards an attempt and posted a +1.1 CPOE. The true version of him is closer to that competent backup than to the Buffalo line. The sack problem is real, though: pressure-to-sack rates near 40% now in back-to-back years, and poor in 2020 and 2022 as well. He is a playable emergency option behind the league's best defense. He is not someone to build a passing game around.

strengths.title: Middle-of-the-field timing still works
strengths.body: Between the hashes he has been a functional passer: positive EPA, a 55% success rate and near-expected accuracy. Those throws come on schedule, inside the structure, to Hockenson and Jefferson in the seams. That fits his career profile as a rhythm thrower. It is his most repeatable skill and the one any spot start should be built around.

strengths.title: Shows up in high-leverage snaps
strengths.body: The red zone (+0.539 EPA over 7 plays), close fourth quarters (+0.346, 77.8% completions over 10 plays) and third down (+1.1 CPOE) have all been better than his overall line. The samples are tiny, so this is a hint, not a trait. Still, it suggests the floor in a must-convert spot is higher than his overall CPOE implies.

strengths.title: Recent baseline is far better
strengths.body: Last season, in the same offense, he was a roughly average passer: 65.1% completions, 7.2 yards per attempt and a positive CPOE. That came over five games, more than this year's sample. It argues that much of the 2026 collapse is one bad afternoon against Buffalo rather than a cliff.

concerns.title: Accuracy has fallen off a shelf
concerns.body: A -15.41 CPOE and a league-worst 28.1% bad-throw rate are not just low completion rates on deep throws. He has missed at every depth, including -16.4 CPOE on throws under 10 air yards. Part of it is self-inflicted aggression: forcing tight windows while chasing the Buffalo game. Expect partial recovery toward his 2025 form, but his career bad-throw ranks say he will never be a precision passer.

concerns.title: Outside throws have been dead
concerns.body: Throws outside the numbers to the right have produced -0.271 EPA a play, and to the left he is completing a third of his passes with a -26.1 CPOE. Those are the throws that require anticipation and arm placement against tighter coverage. With Addison and Jennings out, the outside receivers he would be throwing to are thinner still.

concerns.title: Sacks without the legs to offset
concerns.body: His 9.9% sack rate ranks 42nd and nearly 39% of pressures end in sacks. That is not new: 2025, 2022 and 2020 all ranked poorly by this measure. What changed is that he no longer gets anything back with his legs, with designed runs losing value and scrambles going nowhere. Holding the ball has become all cost.

trend.note: His passing EPA went from +5.1 in Week 1 relief to roughly break-even in the Chicago win, then to -18.4 against Buffalo. Cousins started the next game, and Wentz is now listed third.

nextGame.headline: QB3 at San Francisco: soft pass rush, depleted receivers
nextGame.body:
If Wentz plays in San Francisco, the matchup is mixed. The 49ers are the league's least disruptive pass rush, with a 4.5% sack rate that ranks 31st. They are also soft underneath (short-throw EPA allowed ranks 24th), exactly where his game still functions. They are stingy deep, though, and the 49ers own the league's best offense, so a trailing script would push him into the aggressive downfield throws that sank him against Buffalo.

Availability is the whole story, starting with his own. He is listed QB3 behind Cousins with Murray out, so he plays only if something goes wrong. Minnesota is also missing Addison (thumb surgery), Jennings and, for now, Hockenson, who is expected to make progress toward Sunday. That leaves Jefferson and the backup tight end Josh Oliver as the receivers he has had any success with. On the 49ers' side, starting corner Renardo Green (93% of snaps) is questionable with a back injury. Two rotational defensive tackles are on IR, which further thins an already light pass rush. The forecast is early but calls for a chance of drizzle and gusts near 18 mph, worth monitoring for a passer this inaccurate rather than a reason to change the read.

keyMatchups.title: No pass rush to fear
keyMatchups.body: San Francisco rarely gets home, and two interior linemen are on IR. For a quarterback whose pressures turn into sacks at a high rate, a clean pocket is the best possible setting. It would let him throw on rhythm to the middle of the field.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots run into strength
keyMatchups.body: The 49ers rank 4th in deep EPA allowed, and his 20-plus-yard throws have been negative with a third completed. If the game gets away, his forcing tendency meets the one part of this defense that is sound.

keyMatchups.title: Shootout script vs SF offense
keyMatchups.body: Minnesota is a 3-point road underdog against the top offense by EPA. Even the Vikings' top-ranked defense may not keep this low-scoring, and his worst football has come with the game in the balance.

nextGame.watch: Whether Wentz is even active, and if Cousins struggles, whether Wentz is used as the next man up or stays third string.

restOfSeason.body:
Wentz's season now depends on other people's health. Murray's estimated return is late November, Cousins started Week 10, and Wentz sits third. The likeliest path is few or no snaps. If he is called on, expect something between his 2025 form and his 2026 starts: completion rate recovering into the mid-to-high 50s as the Buffalo game stops dominating the sample, but sacks staying high and almost nothing as a runner. His touchdown rate, which ranks 21st, rests on a Week 1 relief game and seven red-zone plays and should drift down.

A spot start is survivable for Minnesota because its defense ranks first and wins low-scoring games, as the 9-3 Chicago win showed. Even then, he caps the offense at roughly 120 to 200 passing yards in a start.
swingFactors: Murray's hamstring timeline and Cousins' hold on the job
Return of Addison, Jennings and Hockenson
Whether he stops forcing tight-window throws

confidence.note: 64 attempts across three scattered games; currently QB3 with no defined role.
